description: The Central Pollution Control Board of India publishes the status of sewage treatment plants, with a link to the National Inventory of Sewage Treatment Plants 2021; the page was updated on 8 March 2021. The page text states that domestic sewage from cities and towns is the largest source of water pollution in India and tabulates, on a 2001 population basis, the number of Class I cities and Class II towns by size, their estimated sewage generation of 29,129 MLD, installed treatment capacity of 6,190 MLD, the capacity gap in cities with and without plants, and 1,742.6 MLD of capacity planned or under construction. Coverage is India. Access is free as a PDF report and a web table. Caveats: the page table uses 2001 population figures, the inventory report itself was not read, and no licence is stated. Simulation uses: sewage treatment capacity and gaps for wastewater network and plant planning and receiving-water pollution scenarios. Related records: ANA Atlas Esgotos (data-ana-atlas-esgotos-brazil-wastewater-treatment-plants) and HydroWASTE (data-hydrowaste).
